messages.author: 1e55c83b1f50d96a
messages.subject: Error in read.capthist
parts:
Hi all,

I have a problem trying to run the function read.capthist for SECR. It keeps coming up with this error: 
Error in rep(NA, nfield - nvar) : invalid 'times' argument
In addition: Warning message:
In max(do.call(count.fields, countargs)) :
  no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf

I'm using the polygon detector type to determine the density of cats within a particular search area. I read an earlier thread in www.phidot.org with a similar error and the issue was resolved by using a .csv file but it didn't work for me. The CRS for the coordinates of the polygon vertices is SVY21. I attached my R script and the associated .txt and .csv files for reference. The R version I'm using is 4.0.2.

I have 2 questions: what does the error mean and how can I resolve this? Any help is much appreciated.
Best,
Malcolm

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Error in read.capthist
parts:
Hi Malcolm
I think you got needlessly tangled up here. Do not put your data in the package extdata folder. The example in secr-datainput.pdf goes there just to retrieve some demo data that is distributed with the package. The only tricky thing is that for csv and text files secr requires that you explicitly to skip the header line (as in the xlsx example in that document). In this instance the error message is not useful, but that's R for you.
Murray

Try this:

library(secr)
setwd('d:/density users/malcolm soh')   # or your data folder
h23hr <- read.capthist(captfile = "H23hrcapt.csv", trapfile = "H23hrpoly.csv",
    fmt = "XY", detector = "polygon", skip = 1)
# No errors found :-)
plot(h23hr, tracks = TRUE)
summary(h23hr)
# Object class       capthist
# Detector type      polygon
# Number vertices    7
# Number polygons    1
# Total area         4.322366 ha
# x-range            33613.41 33832.1 m
# y-range            33434.97 33654.24 m
#
# Counts by occasion
# 1 2 3 4 Total
# n                 5 4 5 5    19
# u                 5 0 1 0     6
# f                 1 1 0 4     6
# M(t+1)            5 5 6 6     6
# losses            0 0 0 0     0
# detections        5 4 5 5    19
# detectors visited 1 1 1 1     4
# detectors used    1 1 1 1     4
